Apply eligibility rules and account for every row that leaves

Source: R/cleaning.R
mm_clean.Rd

Each rule is a named one-sided formula evaluated in the cohort. Rows where it is TRUE continue; rows where it is FALSE are excluded and attributed to that rule by name.

Usage

mm_clean(cohort, rules = list(), label = "rows as supplied")

Arguments

cohort

The raw cohort.

rules

Named list of one-sided formulas, each evaluating to a logical vector over cohort, as ~ age >= 40. A formula is used rather than a bare expression so that nothing is evaluated before the cohort is in scope. The names become the ledger's labels, so they should read as the criterion they express.

label

What the rows are, for the ledger's opening line.

Value

An object of class mm_cohort, holding data and ledger.

Details

The ledger is the point. A cohort count that cannot be reconciled against the raw export is the commonest reason a published flow diagram does not add up, so this function refuses to return one: rows in must equal rows out plus every exclusion, and the check is an error rather than a note.

A rule that evaluates to NA for a row is not a pass. A row whose eligibility cannot be determined is excluded under its own heading, because treating unknown as eligible and treating it as ineligible are different studies and the difference belongs in the diagram.

Nothing here imputes, recodes or drops a column. Missingness is described by mm_eda() and handled at imputation, where the choice is explicit.

Examples

raw <- mm_synthetic_cohort(n = 300, seed = 1)
clean <- mm_clean(raw, rules = list(
  "aged 40 or over" = ~ age >= 40,
  "plausible BMI"   = ~ bmi >= 16 & bmi <= 55
))
clean
#> <mm_cohort>  300 in, 284 out, 16 excluded
#>      300  rows as supplied
#>      -10  aged 40 or over (did not meet the criterion)
#>      290  remaining
#>       -6  plausible BMI (did not meet the criterion)
#>      284  remaining
clean$ledger
#>   step             rule n_before n_excluded n_after                     reason
#> 1    0 rows as supplied       NA         NA     300            starting cohort
#> 2    1  aged 40 or over      300         10     290 did not meet the criterion
#> 3    2    plausible BMI      290          6     284 did not meet the criterion
